findings.evidence: Specialization.lean:116-128 vs IntegralCoefficients.lean:121-134: both obtain a right inverse of the same `IsUnit f`, build `evalIntSeries _ _ f * evalIntSeries _ _ g = 1` via `← map_mul`, and conclude by `le_antisymm` against `norm_evalIntSeries_le_one`; the new version differs only by carrying an extra left factor `x := (q : K)`, and holds for arbitrary `x` with the same proof.
findings.fix: In `TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/InfiniteSum/IntegralCoefficients.lean`, replace `norm_evalIntSeries_eq_one_of_isUnit` with `theorem norm_mul_evalIntSeries_of_isUnit (x q : K) (hq : ‖q‖ < 1) {f : ℤ⟦X⟧} (hf : IsUnit f) : ‖x * evalIntSeries q hq f‖ = ‖x‖`, proved by the `le_antisymm`/`norm_mul_le_of_le` argument currently inlined here; then `norm_tateCurveAt_Δ` is `rw [tateCurveAt, WeierstrassCurve.map_Δ, hΔ, map_mul, evalIntSeries_X]; exact norm_mul_evalIntSeries_of_isUnit _ _ hq ((isUnit_iff_constantCoeff (φ := u)).mpr (by simp [hu]))`. Per the no-compatibility policy, drop the now-redundant `= 1` form (or keep it as a one-line corollary with `x = 1` if a caller appears).
findings.issue: Lines 116-128 inline a general fact about `evalIntSeries` — for `IsUnit f`, `‖x * evalIntSeries q hq f‖ = ‖x‖` in any complete ultrametric `NormedCommRing` with `NormOneClass` — specialized to `x = q`, `f = u`. The argument (take a right inverse, `norm_mul_le_of_le` in both directions) uses nothing about the Tate curve, so it is stated at the elliptic-curve level instead of the evaluation level. It also strictly generalizes the existing `norm_evalIntSeries_eq_one_of_isUnit` (`IntegralCoefficients.lean:121`, the `x = 1` case via `NormOneClass`), which this PR leaves with zero callers in the repo: `grep -rn norm_evalIntSeries_eq_one_of_isUnit code/` hits only its own declaration and proof.

summary: The generalization direction is right and the coefficient identities are now correctly derived from the formal ones. But the general normed-ring fact driving the new discriminant proof is inlined as a special case in the elliptic-curve file, while the strictly weaker general lemma it subsumes sits unused in IntegralCoefficients.lean.
